task_version.definition:
@kbench.task(
    name="deadline-math-hard-reasoned",
    # Literal y de 255 caracteres como mÃ¡ximo: Kaggle rechaza la task si no.
    description=(
        "Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when "
        "the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth "
        "computed with zoneinfo."
    ),
)
def deadline_math(llm) -> float:
    passed = 0
    for case in CASE_SETS[SET]:
        response, output_tokens = ask(llm, case)
        answer = parse_answer(response)
        # Sin lÃ­nea final y al borde del lÃ­mite: se cortÃ³. Cuenta como fallo, pero se marca para el anÃ¡lisis.
        truncated = answer is None and output_tokens >= 0.95 * MAX_TOKENS
        kbench.assertions.assert_equal(
            case.expected, answer,
            expectation=f"[{case.category}] {case.id}: {case.statement} -> {case.reader} = {case.expected}"
            + (f" (truncated at max_tokens={MAX_TOKENS})" if truncated else ""),
        )
        passed += answer == case.expected
    # ProporciÃ³n de aciertos: Kaggle aÃºn no muestra Â«aciertos de totalÂ» (lee la tupla como valor Â± intervalo).
    return passed / len(CASE_SETS[SET])

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“Six days from today” matches **Friday, October 30, 2026**.  
The stated deadline is **Friday at 11:59 PM PT**.

On **October 30, 2026**, Pacific Time is **PDT (UTC−7)** because U.S. daylight saving time hasn’t ended yet.  
Madrid on that date is on **CET (UTC+1)** because Spain has already switched back after the last Sunday in October.

So Madrid is **8 hours ahead** of Pacific Time.

- **2026-10-30 23:59 PT**
- plus 8 hours
- = **2026-10-31 07:59** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is on Pacific Time. On **Monday, November 2, 2026**, Los Angeles is still observing **PDT (UTC−7)**, while Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)** after Europe’s clock change the week before.

That makes Madrid **8 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.

So:
- **Monday, Nov 2, 2026, 10:00 AM in Los Angeles**
- plus **8 hours**
- = **Monday, Nov 2, 2026, 6:00 PM in Madrid**

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The start is already given in your local time: Madrid, Spain.

Add exactly 48 hours to:
- Start: Saturday, 2026-10-24 18:00

48 hours = 2 days, so the end is:
- Monday, 2026-10-26 18:00 in Madrid local time

(That weekend includes the daylight saving time change in Spain early on Sunday, but since the start time is explicitly in Madrid local time and the event lasts exactly 48 hours, the local end time is still 18:00 on Monday.)

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid observes CET/CEST, while “PT” means Pacific Time (Los Angeles time), which in late October can be either PDT or PST depending on the exact date.

- Start: October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT
- Add 72 hours: October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT

On October 29, 2026:
- Pacific Time is on PDT (UTC−7), because the U.S. has not switched off daylight saving yet.
- Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), because Spain has already switched back by then.

So Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT at that moment.

10:00 AM PT + 8 hours = 18:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“ET” in late October means **Eastern Time**, which is still on **EDT (UTC−4)** until early November.

- Submissions close: **2026-10-31 23:59 ET**
- Add 36 hours: **2026-11-02 11:59 ET**

Madrid on **2026-11-02** is on **CET (UTC+1)**, because Spain has already ended daylight saving time the day before.

Time difference then:
- **ET (UTC−5 on Nov 2? careful)**

At the moment of the announcement, Eastern Time has also switched from EDT to **EST (UTC−5)**, because the US changes clocks on **2026-11-01**. So:

- **2026-11-02 11:59 EST**
- Madrid is **CET (UTC+1)**
- Difference = **6 hours ahead**

So the announcement in Madrid is:

**2026-11-02 17:59**

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Unix timestamp **1791788340** corresponds to **2026-10-12 00:59:00 UTC**.

Tokyo, Japan is **UTC+9** year-round, so add 9 hours:

**2026-10-12 09:59** in Tokyo local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 09:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The timestamp ends with **Z**, which means **UTC**.

On **2026-10-25**, Madrid is observing **CET/CEST changeover day**. By **02:30 UTC**, Spain has already switched from **CEST (UTC+2)** to **CET (UTC+1)**, so Madrid local time is **UTC+1** at that moment.

So:

- **2026-10-25 02:30 UTC**
- plus **1 hour**
- = **2026-10-25 03:30** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.

At that date, **Pacific Time** will still be **PDT (UTC−7)**, so:

- **2026-10-25 11:59 PM Pacific Time**
- = **2026-10-26 06:59 UTC**

Madrid switches from CEST to CET on the **last Sunday of October**, and by **06:59 UTC on October 26**, Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

So the local time in Madrid is:

- **2026-10-26 07:59**

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the US ends daylight saving time on **Sunday, November 1, 2026**.

By **12:00 noon Eastern Time** on that date, the Eastern time zone is back on **EST (UTC-5)**.

Lima, Peru stays on **PET (UTC-5)** year-round, so it has the **same UTC offset** as Eastern Time after the DST change.

So the deadline in Lima is the **same local clock time**:

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means **Anywhere on Earth**, which is effectively the last place on Earth where the date still exists: **UTC−12:00**.

So:

- **2026-12-31 24:00 AoE** = **2027-01-01 00:00** in **UTC−12:00**
- Converting to UTC: add 12 hours → **2027-01-01 12:00 UTC**
- Tokyo is **JST = UTC+9** year-round
- Add 9 hours → **2027-01-01 21:00 JST**

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney on October 5, 2026 is in AEDT (UTC+11) due to daylight saving time. New York on October 5, 2026 is in EDT (UTC-4).

So New York is 15 hours behind Sydney that day.

5:00 PM in Sydney on 2026-10-05 minus 15 hours = 2:00 AM in New York on 2026-10-05.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
